metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Agricultural Fields
metas.note: Due to Alaska’s very cold climate; agricultural fields are mainly found in the south of the state, mostly in the Matanuska Valley and Kenai Peninsula.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Alexander Archipelago (Gen 2)
metas.note:
The Alaskan towns in the Alexander Archipelago, on the British Columbia border have a unique look. Tall mountains with lush green forests can be seen in the background, with the majority of buildings made of wood. In addition, Generation 2 coverage is often overcast and misty.

NOTE: Coastal areas of Oregon and Washington can have a similar appearance in terms of landscape and foliage.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Alexander Archipelago Landscape
metas.note:
The Alaskan towns in the Alexander Archipelago, on the British Columbia border have a unique look. Tall mountains with lush green forests can be seen in the background, with the majority of buildings made of wood.

NOTE: Coastal areas of Oregon and Washington can have a similar appearance in terms of landscape and foliage.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Denali Highway
metas.note: The Denali highway (8), stretching from Cantwell to Paxson in central Alaska, is a mostly gravel highway in the ‘Alaska’ mountain range. This road runs generally east to west, is covered in the generation 2 camera, and was taken in late summer, so wildflowers and green shrubby plants are common.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Juneau
metas.note: Juneau, Alaska’s Capital city, is the largest settlement in the Alaskan panhandle. Therefore, it is much more ‘built up’ than other towns in this area. The city is surrounded by heavily forested mountains and hills.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Kenai Peninsula
metas.note: The Kenai peninsula can be recognized by its massive amount of fireweed along the roads. Most of the coverage is Gen 3 Autumn. Along AK-1 you will often see a bay to the west with mountains on the other side.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Max North Landscape
metas.note: The North end of the Dalton Highway (11) features a flat and snowy landscape and an overcast sky. A small ridge of hills can be seen to the west of the highway in certain spots.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Prudhoe Bay
metas.note: Prudhoe Bay, the northernmost town in America covered by street view, can be recognized by cold, dead landscape, overcast clouds and lack of tall buildings. A second Google car can sometimes be seen.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Steese Highway
metas.note: The Steese Highway (6) is a gravel highway that goes from Fairbanks to the town of ‘Central.’ Similar to the Denali highway, this road runs generally east to west and is covered in generation 2. The difference, however, is that the mountains along this road are noticeably lower than the ones adjacent to the Denali Highway.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Suburban Area with Mountains
metas.note: Suburban areas around Anchorage feature wide roads, commercial districts, and sometimes heavy traffic. Mountains can commonly be seen in the distance.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Suburban Area without Mountains
metas.note: Suburban areas around Anchorage feature wide roads, commercial districts, and sometimes heavy traffic. Compared to Anchorage, the landscape is flatter.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Tundra
metas.note: Most of interior and northern Alaska lies in subarctic or tundra climate zones. These areas feature relatively low amounts of forest undergrowth and shorter trees.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Urban Coverage
metas.note: The only two major urban areas in Alaska are Anchorage and Fairbanks.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Afono Bay
metas.note: Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards straight North. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Camel Rock
metas.note:
Behold: The Camel Rock. Two little peaks reaching into the ocean.

It is marked as a POI on Google Maps.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - East of Summit 001 - Overcast
metas.note:
This road crosses the district border on the 001. It is characterized through the unique angle and the mountains in the north. Often you can see a unique summit in the west. The driving direction is eastwards.

There is a stretch of the 001 with a similar angle near Malaeimi, but it has a clearly visible valley in the North which is not found on this road.

The road can further be divided as it is overcast in the Western District and sunny in the Eastern District.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - East of Summit 001 - Sunny
metas.note:
This road crosses the district border on the 001. It is characterized through the unique angle and the mountains in the north. Often you can see a unique summit in the west. The driving direction is eastwards.

There is a stretch of the 001 with a similar angle near Malaeimi, but it has a clearly visible valley in the North which is not found on this road.

The road can further be divided as it is overcast in the Western District and sunny in the Eastern District.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Eastern South Coast Road
metas.note:
This long stretch of road (which is probably further regionguessable) is easily recognizable because it has a South Coast and the Car Drives westward (unlike the Western Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your right.

There is one annoying exception, around the POI 'Amouli Beach Fales' east of the town Amouli.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Fagasa Bay
metas.note: Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northwest. Note that Afono is opened towards North proper, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Manu'a - North Coast road (paved)
metas.note: On Manu'a/Olosega (which have a unique car), there are two covered roads with North coast: The roads east and west of the famous bridge. They can easily be differentiated, because the Olosega (east) road is unpaved, while the Manu'a (west) road has concrete pavement.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Manu'a - North Coast road (unpaved)
metas.note: On Manu'a/Olosega (which have a unique car), there are two covered roads with North coast: The roads east and west of the famous bridge. They can easily be differentiated, because the Olosega (east) road is unpaved, while the Manu'a (west) road has concrete pavement.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Manu'a - Ofu
metas.note:
The town Ofu on Manu'a has a West Coast. This road can be distinguished from the West Coast of Olosega, because:

  • It is entirely paved (unlike the town Olosega)
  • It has no Mountain in the North (unlike the paved road north of Olosega).

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Pago Pago Harbour
metas.note: The roads alonog the Pago Pago Harbour are recognizable because they're generally very urban (for American Samoa), and you can often see the harbour when it isn't blocked by buildings.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Tau - Faleasao
metas.note: Faleasao is a little town on Tau (and thus has the Tau car). It has a coast in the North and is otherwise surrounded by mountains. Together with the Tau car, it is unique.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Tutuila - Rte 018
metas.note:
The Rte 018 in Tafuna is urban and uniquely shows this mountain in the North. The alignment is generally North-South. The road has double yellow lines (not that common in AS) and a power line in the East. The driving direction is to the North.

Make sure that parts of the Rte 001 can look similar with a similar road angle. To confirm it's the Rte 018, you can pan exactly North. If you look at the mountain, it's the Rte 018, otherwise it's not.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Tutuila East Coast
metas.note: This is the only part of Tutuila where you can see Coast on the east, without other parts of Tutuila visible. You will often see Aunu'u in the Southeast.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Vatia Bay
metas.note: Vatia Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northeast. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Afono Bay is opened towards North proper.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Western South Coast Road
metas.note:
This road is easily recognizable because it has a South Coast and the Car drives eastward (unlike the Eastern Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your left.

On the eastern south coast road, there is a tiny part that also drives eastward for some reason, which can be baity.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Bahia Blanca Hills
metas.note: Semi-coastal grass hills are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of Bahía Blanca.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Chaco & Formosa Landscape
metas.note: In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Chenque Hill
metas.note: Comodoro Rivadavia is built on the slopes of Chenque hill, making the city recognisable.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Cordoba Mountains
metas.note: These mountains are typically found west of Córdoba.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Flat & Barren Landscape
metas.note: Flat and barren landscapes like this are typically found in central southern Argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Grassland
metas.note: Grassland with a few separated tree plantations is generally found in this area.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Mars Coverage
metas.note: The RP1 in Neuquen has dark, cloudy coverage. It is a dark red dirt road and thus resembles Mars. There is some spill onto the RP7 in the North and the RP10 in the South.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Max South Landscape
metas.note: If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Mountains
metas.note: Far western Argentina typically features a mountainous landscape.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Red Mountains
metas.note: These red mountains are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Red Soil
metas.note: Red soil is typically found in the Misiones province.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Road of Death
metas.note: The western part of the RN65 in western Tucumán can easily be recognized by this bendy unpaved road up in the mountains.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Road of Death - Cloudy
metas.note: The western part of the RN65 in western Tucumán can easily be recognized by this bendy unpaved road up in the mountains with its western part up in the clouds.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Salt Pans
metas.note: Salt pans in Argentina are typically found in Jujuy.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - San Luis Roads
metas.note: Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Small Lakes and Ponds
metas.note: Small lakes near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Talampaya National Park
metas.note: Red soil with a barren landscape and mountain ranges, can often be seen on the RN76 in Parque Nacional Talampaya in western La Rioja.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Ushuaia
metas.note: These snowy mountains to the north can only be found in Ushuaia.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino
metas.note: Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino in northeastern Chubut is surrounded by these rock formations.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino Dam
metas.note: This unique dam with the rock formations typical for Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino can be found west of the town.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Volcanic Rocks
metas.note: These volcanic rocks in Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the RP43 south of Antofagasta de la Sierra in northwestern Catamarca.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Alice Springs
metas.note: Alice Springs, an isolated town in the southern part of the Northern Territory, features distinct orange rocks that can be seen in the distance or at the end of roads.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Cairns Landscape
metas.note: The northern QLD city of Cairns is distinct due to its tropical vegetation and big green mountains around the city.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Darwin Landscape
metas.note: The vegetation in the area surrounding Darwin is extremely distinct. It features dark red soil, as well as rich green grass and trees. The tree trunks are typically black.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Eastern South Australia Landscape
metas.note:
The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has quite dry vegetation and is made up of shrubs and wide cronwed eucalyptus. In addition, the soil is sandy with a white tint.

Western South Australia has a similar landscape, but with orangish soil.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Green & Golden Fields
metas.note: Lush green or golden fields can be found in this band from the south of the Yorke Peninsula to Echuca. In the SA side, the landscape should be drier than the Victorian side and more wide crowned eucalyptus can be seen. On the Victorian side, the trees generally have more leaves and are taller.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Inland New South Wales Landscape
metas.note: The landscape in inland NSW is mostly flat, and the soil gets redder the more inland you go. Vegetation consists of mostly dry pale-green shrubs. Further east and on the Queensland and Victorian borders, the climate gets more temperate but is still quite dry and more eucalyptus trees can be seen, with the soil transitioning into a more sandy colour as well as more hills being visible.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Kangaroo Island Landscape
metas.note:
Kangaroo Island in South Australia tends to have a distinct look. The vegetation mostly consists of bushes and low, stubby eucalyptus trees with puffy clusters of leaves. The orange soil colour is reminiscent of Western Australia.

In addition, the island only has Generation 2 and Generation 4 coverage, with Generation 2 being most common.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Mount Gambier Tree Plantations
metas.note: The area around Mount Gambier, SA features white soil and extensive pine tree plantations, making it recognisable.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Northern Queensland Landscape
metas.note: Coastal northern Queensland is very tropical. Typical vegetation consists of palm trees and dark green vegetation.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Nullarbor Highway
metas.note:
The Nullarbor Highway (Latin for “no tree”) can be easily recognized thanks to the flatness, overall grey look and very low vegetation.

NOTE: Use the road angle or road lines to determine whether you are on the WA or SA side.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Reddish-Orange Soil
metas.note: Western Australia, and especially the Perth area, is known for its reddish-orange soil.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Stuart Highway with Blue Car
metas.note: The Stuart Highway from Alice Springs to around Pimba, SA can be easily recognized by its bright orange dirt, short trees and blue car Generation 4.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Tasmania Landscape
metas.note: Tasmania has a cool temperate climate which is uncommon in the rest of Australia and is comparable to central-southern Chile or New Zealand. Typical landscape consists of green rolling hills that can look dry in winter coverage. Eucalyptus trees can be seen on the side of roads and on hills in the distance. Rural Tasmania is also quite hilly with dense eucalyptus forests making up the landscape.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Termite Hills
metas.note: Termite mounds can sometimes be seen in the Northern Territory and rarely northern WA and QLD. They appear as brown, spiky formations rising out of the ground.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Tom Price Landscape
metas.note: The area around Tom Price can be recognized by its red soil and rocky hills.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Western South Australia Landscape
metas.note:
The area around Warramboo in SA to Madura in WA has a unique landscape. Vegetation is quite dry and is made up of shrubs and wide crowned eucalyptus. In addition, the soil is sandy with a slight orange tint.

The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has a similar landscape, with the same vegetation but usually with whiter soil.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Acre Landscape
metas.note: Acre has a unique landscape of small grass hills and sparsely growing trees. The roads often do not cut around the hills like in most of Brazil, but ride the hills instead. A similar landscape can also be seen near Maraba in the state of Pará.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Amazon Rainforest
metas.note: The Amazon is a dense rainforest that compromises 40% of Brazil's total area. Not many roads are within it, but those that are, mostly go through either biodiverse forest or grassy hills with sparse trees.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Amazonas 319
metas.note: The Amazonas 319 has a very lush, bright green and tropical landscape, as it cuts through the Amazon rainforest. The road is flat and mostly unpaved, featuring bright orange soil. However, closer to Manaus the road becomes paved. There are wooden or ladder poles alongside the entire stretch. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR-163 in Para
metas.note: The Pará section of the 163 is often hilly, curvy, dry, and sometimes hazy. It has a wide range of amazonian vegetation. The road is frequently trafficked, usually by transportation trucks. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR174 in Amazonas
metas.note: This road can be recognized by the Amazonian looking trees and the NW/SE angle. It always has Gen 4 and an exposed, blue car front.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR230 in Amazonas
metas.note: This wide dirt road has Amazonian trees and a blurred car. You will not find other cars on the road. It's the only East-to-West angle road in that area.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR230 in Para
metas.note: This road looks like an Amazonian road with the trees and dense rainforest. It runs east-west, slightly to the south. The road looks like its stained with mud
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR319, North of Porto Velho
metas.note: This road is characterized by it's Amazonian look and the SW-NE road angle. Some sections of this road are overcast and/or showcase a flat landscape.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Caatinga landscape
metas.note: Northeastern Brazil can be identified by its dry soil, shrubs and succulents (the Caatinga landscape).

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Caatinga landscape - rain coverage
metas.note: Northeastern Brazil can be identified by its dry soil, shrubs and succulents (the Caatinga landscape). In rainy season coverage, the shrubs are still recognizable, but can be deceptively green.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Corvo Branco
metas.note: This road in eastern Santa Catarina is characterized by its windyness and by the steep mountains and cliffs along its side. It can feel like your driving with the clouds. The road goes through Corvo Branco which is a famous tourist attraction.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Dunas da Sabiaguaba
metas.note: This road east of Fortaleza is characterized by its unique pavement and the sanddunes along the road.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Exposed Rock
metas.note: Espírito Santo, and the surrounding areas, often have large mountains with exposed rock.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Flat Wetland
metas.note: Coastal regions in Rio Grande do Sul are recognisable due to being a rare flat wetland, which is uncommon in Brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Landbridge in Rio Grande do Sul
metas.note: Recognizable by the swamp-like landscape, the pine trees along the road and the Lagoon It runs at a SE-NW angle.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Noronha Rocks
metas.note: Ilha de Fernando de Noronha is similar in vegetation to NE-Brazil and has large exposed rocks.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - North of Uiramuta road
metas.note: This very unique looking road features rolling hills, which is unusual for the rather flat Roraima. It is a windy dirt road and despite being green, it lacks trees. What seperates this from the road south of Uiramuta is that it's more skinny and steeper.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Rio Grande do Sul Landscape
metas.note: The landscape in Rio Grande do Sul can be hilly or flat with lush, green fields. Southern areas can have some resemblance to Uruguay.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Rollercoaster Road
metas.note: The 364 through Acre is very recognisable due to the rollercoaster-like landscape and road: the road uniquely rides the hills rather than snaking around them. There is usually no traffic, and is covered mostly by Generation 3 with an antenna.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Roraima Landscape
metas.note: Rural locations in Roraima are mostly open grassy plains with large, distant mountains in the background. Occasionally, you are on roads within the mountains. Furthermore, the grass in Roraima is distinctly thin, and grows in bunches.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Serra do Mar
metas.note:
Serra do Mar is a high mountain range that runs close to the coast from Parana to Northern RGDS.

If you have a high altitude road going on the mountains, instead of in the valleys, you're likely here.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - South of Uiramuta
metas.note: This very unique looking road features rolling hills, which is unusual for the rather flat Roraima. It is a windy dirt road and despite being green, it lacks trees. What seperates this from the road south of Uiramuta is that it's less skinny and less steep.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Southeast Hills
metas.note: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo often have rolling grassy hills.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Swampy Road
metas.note: A very swampy road (PA-154) can be found Northwest of Belém. Notably, there are very few trees, and the soil is very red.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Uneven Stone + Corn
metas.note: This beautiful road west of Cascavel and South of Toledo, by the PR-585 is characterized by the uneven red stone pavement and the corn plantation next to it.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A-31
metas.note: The A-31 can be recognised by its high altitude, with a steep drop into a valley to the north. The road also has Gen 3 sunset coverage.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A11 - Barren
metas.note:
After crossing the Lluta River at Poconchile, the Ruta 11 continues out of the valley and up into the mountains. The road is all newly paved (except for a few small segments with ongoing construction) and is generally quite wide. This section of Ruta 11 features:

  • Many concrete barriers (which are often painted yellow), double guardrails, and roadside drainage ways.
  • Maroon-colored asphalt in some places.
  • Mountains are made of light reddish sand with occasional exposed rock. Rounded protrusions are also common

The landscape is bare of vegetation until around Zapahuira, east of which the landscape becomes open and covered with small green bushes.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Chile by Palmerranian

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A11 - Lluta River Valley
metas.note: Along the Lluta River, the Ruta 11 passes through a wide valley lined by sloping, sandy mountains that often feature distinctly round rock protrusions. The valley is home to a large amount of agriculture relative to other parts of the Atacama Desert. You’ll often see sizable green fields lined by bushes, trees, or wooden fences, as well as bunches of planted Mexican fan palms. A railroad track also follows the Lluta River on both sides, so if you’re in a green valley next to both a river and a railroad, you’re almost certainly on Ruta 11.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Chile by Palmerranian

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A11 - Shrubby
metas.note: After crossing the Lluta River at Poconchile, the Ruta 11 continues out of the valley and up into the mountains. The road is all newly paved (except for a few small segments with ongoing construction) and is generally quite wide. The landscape is bare of vegetation until around Zapahuira, east of which the landscape becomes open and covered with small green bushes.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Chile by Palmerranian

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Alto Bio Bio National Reserve
metas.note: A vast, mostly treeless landscape combined with triple yellow lines are seen in Alto Bio Bio National Reserve. While the reserve may look dry, there is a distinct cold and high altitude feel.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Alto Bio Bio National Reserve - Monkey Puzzle Trees
metas.note: A vast, mostly treeless landscape combined with triple yellow lines are seen in Alto Bio Bio National Reserve. While the reserve may look dry, there is a distinct cold and high altitude feel. Monkey puzzles are also seen toward the east.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Alto Loa National Reserve
metas.note: Alto Loa National Reserve can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to snow-capped volcanoes. The reserve does not have any paved roads.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Antofagasta Ridge
metas.note: A rockier, and more uneven ridge can be seen in Antofagasta.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Arica Mountains
metas.note: The province of Arica y Parinacota can be recognized by the smooth, sandy mountains that may look slightly eroded, or have bulbous formations. Valleys are also common, which are rarely seen in other parts of Chile.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Arica Ridge
metas.note: A slight, sandy ridge with a gradual incline can be seen in Arica.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Atacama Desert
metas.note:
The Atacama is an extremely arid desert covering the northern third of Chile. Some parts of it experience the lowest rainfall on the planet. As a result, many locations in this desert are almost completely devoid of any vegetation: you will often just see sand and bare rock without any plants in sight anywhere.

NOTE: The Atacama Desert also covers parts of southern Peru, western Bolivia and northwestern Argentina.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Atacama Mountains
metas.note: These rocky, uneven mountains are most commonly seen in Atacama and northern Coquimbo.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Brownish Red Soil (Gen 3)
metas.note:
This brownish red soil can sometimes be seen in Atacama province.

NOTE: This is most reliable in Generation 3. This soil can be seen in other provinces in Generation 4.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Chiloé Landscape
metas.note:
A rolling, agricultural landscape, comparable to New Zealand, can be seen on Isla Grande de Chiloé.

NOTE: Similar looking landscapes exist in some other parts of the country, but usually more level.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Dry Hills
metas.note: The region around Santiago can be recognized by its semi-arid climate, having dry hills and scattered vegetation.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Eucalyptus
metas.note: Eucalyptus plantations combined with a somewhat dry climate are a good indicator that you are in southwestern Valparaíso.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Iquique Ridge
metas.note: A large, towering ridge can be seen in Iquique.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Lauca National Park
metas.note:
East of Putre, Ruta 11 enters Lauca National Park which has a flatter landscape, with tall snow-capped mountains in the background, and features unique Andean Plateau vegetation like Peruvian feather grass and the recognizable cushion plant yareta (Azorella compacta). You can also find Chilean bollards lining the road, which are extremely rare.

Lauca can look very similar to other areas in the east Andes of northern Chile, but it’s recognizable for the iconic Volcán Parinacota, a tall snow-capped volcano that stands alone and away from other mountain ridges. It’s visible from basically every location in the park, though it can be shrouded by clouds.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Chile by Palmerranian

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Llanos de Challe National Park
metas.note: Llanos de Challe National Park can be recognized by the brown coloured dirt on the roadside, patches of light sand, juniper plants, and dark coloured mountains. The sky is overcast in most of the coverage.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Los Flamencos National Reserve
metas.note: Smooth mountains with a reddish tint are seen in Los Flamencos National Reserve. Salt pans are also a common sight. The reserve uses triple yellow lines.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Los FLamencos National Reserve - Short Dashes
metas.note: Smooth mountains with a reddish tint are seen in Los Flamencos National Reserve. Salt pans are also a common sight. The reserve uses triple yellow lines, with short dashes in the west.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Lush Green Valleys
metas.note: Lush green valleys, with rocky mountains and often overcast coverage, can be seen in southern Los Lagos and northern Aysén.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Maule Landscape
metas.note: Compared to the area around Santiago, the Maule province has a similar look. However, it has a Mediterranean climate, and is generally greener.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Narrow Roads & Trees
metas.note: Narrow roads with trees on both sides can commonly be seen in the provinces of Bio Bio and Araucania.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Nevado Tres Cruces National Park
metas.note: In the west, Nevado Tres Cruces National Park can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to a line of mountains. The sand has a reddish tint.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Nevado Tres Cruces National Park - Snow
metas.note: In the east of this park, the Google Car drives up a mountain pass with views of lightly snow-capped volcanoes and snow on the side of the road. The roads in the National Park are paved.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Pampa del Tamarugal
metas.note: The northern section of Pampa del Tamarugal National Reserve can be recognized by the Tamarugo trees lining the road. The road itself is mediocre quality, and in a consistent north-west direction.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Pan de Azucar National Park
metas.note: Pan de Azucar National Park can be recognized by the brown coloured dirt on the roadside, patches of light sand, little vegetation, and dark coloured mountains. The sky is overcast in most of the coverage

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Puyehue National Park
metas.note: Puyehue National Park can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding the road. The pavement itself has triple yellow lines, and tar snakes are frequently seen.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Puyehue National Park - Dead Trees
metas.note: Puyehue National Park can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding the road. The pavement itself has triple yellow lines, and tar snakes are frequently seen. In the east, many dead trees can be seen with a lack of leaves.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Ruta 1
metas.note: Ruta 1 is a coastal road that is easily recognized by the wall of mountains to the east, and the Pacific Ocean to the west. This image shows the various weather conditions faced on the road to help you make closer guesses.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Ruta 181
metas.note: Ruta 181 leading up to Alto Bio Bio National Reserve has triple yellow lines, looks similar to the reserve but with more vegetation.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Ruta 41 - White Lines
metas.note: Part of Ruta 41 is located in a valley, with snowy mountains seen in the distance. Many trees and vineyards can commonly be seen toward the west. Triple white lines west of the middle between Balala and Miraflores.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Ruta 41 - Yellow Lines
metas.note: Part of Ruta 41 is located in a valley, with snowy mountains seen in the distance. Many trees and vineyards can commonly be seen toward the west. Triple yellow lines east of the middle between Balala and Miraflores.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Villa O'Higgins
metas.note: O’Higgins can be recognized by the large mountains to the east, often casting a shadow over the town. To the west, snow-capped mountains are seen further in the distance.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Deep grey & stony soil in Gen 3
metas.note: This type of soil can be found in towns near the pacific coast.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - East of Andes Landscape
metas.note:
East of the Andes lies a vast lowland called Llanos. It is characterised by open tropical grasslands, savannas with scattered trees, small areas of forest and seasonal flooding.

Since it's to the east of the Andes, you may see mountains in the west, but never in the east.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Guatape Hill
metas.note: This striking cone-shaped mountain can often be seen from the surrounding area of Guatape.
metas.footer: Source: Tipp des Tages on the German Discord Server

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Guaviare Orange Road
metas.note: The only road in Guaviare goes from to Guaviare (city), and continues south up until Vda. El Trueno. It can be recognized by the orange-looking dust on the road.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - La Guajira
metas.note: This landscape is typical of the far Northern province of La Guajira: extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Northern Landscape
metas.note: The Northern part of the country is characterised by white, sandy soil and an arid landscape.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Paramos
metas.note:
Paramos refers to alpine tundra ecosystems located in the mountains. These kinds of regions are easy to guess by how little vegetation grows here. The best clue is these odd looking pants. ( giant rosette plants ).

Note by MB: In my experience, this appears most commonly south of Bogota, still in the capital district.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Pasto Hills
metas.note:
In southern Colombia, around the city of Pasto, there are hilly fields that are unique in that they are bordered by hedges. The hedges are very thick and form very distinctive lines on the hills. It almost gives off a “British” vibe. If you are sure that it is Colombia, this is a very good meta, but such fields with hedges also occur in Ecuador.

!! In very rare cases, such hedges on hills can also occur in other parts of Colombia. !!
metas.footer: Source: Tipp des Tages on the German Discord Server

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Santa Rosalia
metas.note: Santa Rosalia is the only town covered in Vichada. So if you see red/orange dirt in an urban Gen 4 loc, you should go there.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Swamp Road + Extremely Sunny
metas.note: If you see a swamp road with extremely sunny coverage, you're probably on the 74 in Sucre.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Swamp Roads
metas.note: The 74, the 78 and a few other roads more north have very swampy parts, you can see on the map where these are by zooming.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - 78 west of Pailitas
metas.note: This road is characterised by low clouds and a towering mountain in the east.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - Ruta 90 Landbridge
metas.note:
You can recognise the narrow Ruta 90 landbridge between Barranquilla and Cienaga thanks to the dashed yellow lines and shallow bodies of water next to the road. Open ocean can often be seen to the north.

NOTE: In the older Generation 3 coverage, you will also see tall mountains in the distance.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - Uribia to Puerto Boliviar
metas.note: You can often recognise the Uribia-Puerto Bolivar road because of La Guajira landscape (extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti), the straightness and the train track always present to the East.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Vichada Red Dirt
metas.note: Vichada is characterize by hazy Gen 4 coverage and Red Dirt.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: France - Landscape - British Hedges
metas.note:
Rural roads surrounded by hedges blocking the view, reminiscent of the British Isles, are primarily found in the northwest, particularly in Normandy.

NOTE: Hedges by themselves are not sufficient for recognizing this area and are common all over France.

metas.name: France - Landscape - Cote d'Azur
metas.note: The French Riviera (Cote d'Azur) will mirror many characteristics of Monaco. Rich areas with planted palms and light coloured multi story buildings with wide balconies are good indications you’re in this area, with the rest of the southern coast and Corsican Bastia sharing similar vibes.

metas.name: France - Landscape - La Beauce
metas.note:
La Beauce is one of the flattest regions of France, located South of Paris.

Apart from the flatness of the area, the important thing to notice about the fields in the Beauce region is that they are industrialized. You will not see hedges around the fields like you could see in the West of France. So, if you see very flat and industrialized fields with potatoes or cereals, you can be in this area. Still, the Paris hedge remains good because there are many fields North and East of Paris (but you will never get a 5K by guessing Paris out of fields).
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Landscape - Mountains
metas.note: The tallest mountains are found in the southeast and on the Spanish border.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Alps
metas.note: The German Alps is the most mountainous region in Germany, it is mostly concentrated on the Austrian Border.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Flat Landscape
metas.note: The North and especially Northwest of Germany is very flat.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Hilliness
metas.note: Central Germany is hilly.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Regensburg Plains & Ridge
metas.note: The flat plains southeast of Regensburg can be recognised by the slight ridge often visible to the northeast. The plains themselves are flat, and quite agricultural.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Sylt
metas.note:
The shrub and sand covered hills are unique to the island of Sylt. And like the rest of the North Frisian Islands, rock walls, brick houses, and thatched roofs are common.

NOTE: Some parts of Sylt look more generic, but still very flat.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Central Maui
metas.note: The Island of Maui sits southeast of Molokaʻi. In the centre of the island, you will find somewhat flat grasslands. It has the very recognizable West Maui Mountains to the west, and Haleakala to the east.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Coastal Big Island
metas.note:
The coastal areas of the island of Hawai’i are where most of the towns and built-up areas on the island are located. These areas are typically more lush and have more trees and fern plants than the interior.

Note by MB: There is a similar road, the Hana Highway on Maui, which is more narrow and has narrower shoulders than the typical road on Hawai'i.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Coastal Lana'i
metas.note: Towards the coasts of the island of Lānaʻi, hills dotted with dry grass and shrubby vegetation are commonly seen. These areas are very rural with few buildings.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Coastal Maui
metas.note: Coastal areas of Maui are noticeably lush and green. Banana plants, palm trees, and views of the mountains are all common.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - East Molokai Volcano
metas.note:
Rather flat and wide volcano, making it's shape quite unique.

As the name suggests, it's found in the East of Moloka'i island.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Flat Forest
metas.note: Rural roads going through forests within a flat landscape are commonly found south of the city of Hilo, on the island of Hawaiʻi.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Haleakala Foothills
metas.note: The area near Kula is at the foot of Haleakala and often looks over the rest of the island.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hana Highway (North)
metas.note:
The Hana Highway runs along the coast of Maui and is narrow and lush in the North.

Note by MB: Note that unlike in the picture, Hana Highway also has center lines on some parts. That creates a possible toss-up with Hawai'i island. However, Hana Highway is more narrow and has very narrow shoulders, unlike most roads on Hawai'i.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hana Highway (South)
metas.note:
The Hana Highway runs along the coast of Maui and is narrow. In the south, the landscape is fairly open and you can often see the southern coast, as no trees are in the way.

Note by MB: Note that unlike in the picture, Hana Highway also has center lines on some parts. That creates a possible toss-up with Hawai'i island. However, Hana Highway is more narrow and has very narrow shoulders, unlike most roads on Hawai'i.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hawaiian Lattice
metas.note: The infamous 'Hawaiian lattice' can be recognized by the volcanic soil and rocks that are abundant in the region. Volcanic vegetation can also be seen lining the roads. Note that the angle of the roads is a big clue for the area, and that this lattice was built on the slope of Mauna Loa.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hilo
metas.note:
Hilo fits nicely into the coastal Hawai'i landscape (lush and somewhat built up). What makes it unique is the grid format of many of its roads. You can also sometimes see Mauna Kea in the west.

Note by MB: Other grids also exist on Hawaii island (notably Hawaiian Lattice, and the area south of Hilo), but they look very different. Each has their own meta describing them.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Honolulu
metas.note: Honolulu, located on southern Oʻahu, is by far the largest city and urban area in Hawaii. If you are in a dense urban area and can see tall buildings, you will always be in or near Honolulu.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Houses on Hills
metas.note: In most of Hawaii, houses are built on flat plains. If you see Houses on hillsides, you are most likely around the Ko'olau range in eastern Oahu, often in suburbs of Honolulu.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hualalai
metas.note: Hualalaei (a large mountain) rises to the east of Kona.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Interior Big Island
metas.note:
The Island of Hawai’i (also referred to as The Big Island) is both the largest and farthest southeast island with Street View coverage in the state. The interior areas feature rolling, grassy plains and volcanic rocks. You can typically see one or more of the island’s volcanoes from the road.

What sets apart the mountains on this island is that they are more sloping and gradual than on other islands.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Kauai
metas.note:
The Island of Kauai is the furthest west island in Hawaii with official Google coverage. This island has deep red soil and has large rugged hills with lush, jungle-like vegetation. This island also has exclusively Generation 3 and Smallcam coverage.

NOTE: Other islands such as Maui and Molokaʻi have similar soil colours, but the hillsides on them will typically have less dense vegetation.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Kaunakakai
metas.note: The town of Kaunakakai is the largest settlement on the Island of Molokaʻi. It is the only area on the island with an ‘urban’ vibe.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Lana'i
metas.note: The Island of Lānaʻi is a small, yet distinct island that lies just south of Moloka’i. A volcano is found just east of the centre of the island, adjacent to the town of Lānaʻi. In this area, tall Cook pines are abundant. In addition, some main roads near the centre of the island are lined with younger Cook pines.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Maui West Coast
metas.note: West Maui can often see Molokai and/or Lanai to the west. The northern part of the west coast has the West Maui Mountains rising to the east.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Mauna Loa Observatory Road
metas.note:
This road "looks like Mars", and has large volcanic rocks on its sides.

Note by MB: Unlike the road on Red Hill, this road does not have center lines.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Moloka'i
metas.note:
The Island of Molokaʻi is just southeast of the Island of Oʻahu. This island features deep red soil, dry-looking vegetation, and a prominent volcano on the eastern end of the island. Molokaʻi is also very sparsely populated. This island only has Generation 3 and Smallcam coverage.

Note by MB: In the newest smallcam coverage, the island doesn't look as dry as in Gen 3 (due to different season).

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - O'ahu
metas.note: The Island of Oʻahu lies southeast of Kauai. It is known for being home to the Honolulu urban area. It also is home to steep, lush hills, which can be commonly seen from all around the island, especially in Honolulu’s suburbs. Generation 4 coverage is common on Oʻahu.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Red Hill
metas.note:
The Red Hill can easily be recognised by this unique barren, rocky landscape. Due to the high altitude, clouds are usually visible below you.

Note by MB: In newer smallcam coverage the hill looks not that red, but the coverage is still recognizable. Also, unlike the Mauna Lea observatory road on Hawai'i, this road has yellow center lines.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Seaview Road
metas.note: The road around and east of Seaview (Hawai'i island) is very distinct, as it combines the volcanic rock landscape with water immediately to the South.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Volcanic Rock
metas.note: Hawaii island has the only currently active volcano and is the most recently formed island, so lots of volcanic rock is common.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Akureyri
metas.note: Akureyri is the second-biggest city in Iceland and is located in a North-South oriented valley, along the western edge of the bay. The city features mountains ranges to the east and west, making it recognisable.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Akureyri Mountains
metas.note: The mountains west of Akureyri contain many valleys, sandwiched between tall, often slightly snowcapped peaks. Most of these valleys generally face north to northeast.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Eiðar Valley
metas.note: The wide valley around Eiðar is slightly hilly and agricultural, with tall, snowy peaks visible in the distance on either side, to the east and northwest, respectively.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Flat-Topped Mountains
metas.note: The Westfjords region features numerous narrow fjords, surrounded by moderately tall, and mostly flat-topped mountains.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Fog
metas.note: Very foggy coverage can be found around the town of Bakkagerði, in northeastern Iceland. The fog can also be seen from a distance.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Glaciers
metas.note: The southern coast of Iceland features some impressive glaciers visible from the ring road, spilling into the sea from the Vatnajökull ice cap.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Hallormsstaður Valley
metas.note: The valley around Hallormsstaður has a distinct northeast/southwest angle with low-lying mountains on either side, a wide river flowing through it, and an unusual amount of trees for Iceland. Some of the sideroads are in the forests.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Heimaey
metas.note: The Island of Heimaey can easily be recognised by seeing these ragged rocky cliffs overlooking the town of Vestmannaeyjabær. Similar cliffs can be seen on the islands off the coast.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Inland Iceland
metas.note: Barren landscapes consisting mostly of dark volcanic gravel, with little to no vegetation or signs of life, are typical of the inland regions of Iceland. Most such covered roads are located in the east.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Large Jagged Mountains
metas.note: The far east of the country is also home to several fjords. What distinguishes them from the Westfjords are the generally larger and more jagged mountains.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Reykjavík
metas.note:
Reykjavík is the capital and by far the largest city in Iceland. The city is mostly flat with slight hills, and is located on the south side of a bay. It is most recognizable as it is significantly larger than other Icelandic cities, with a large urban area and “bigger city” feel.

NOTE: The city of Akureyri can feel urban in some places. You can distinguish it from Reykjavik as it has mountains to the east and west.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Selfoss Mountain
metas.note: You can recognise the area near the town of Selfoss from its distinct flat-ridge mountain. Due to the otherwise flat landscape, this mountain can be seen from a wide area.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Southwest Farmland
metas.note:
The Southwest agricultural area in Iceland can be identified by its relatively flat farmland landscape scattered with numerous farmsteads, fields, meadows and grasslands.

NOTE: Although there are other smaller agricultural areas in Iceland, mountains in this area tend to be quite distant, making it unique.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Amygdaloidal Basalt
metas.note:
This is a volcanic rock, which is recognizable by it's dark color with white mineral patches on it.

It is mostly found between Pune and Jalgaon.

It's important to note that this rock alone, without the mineral patches is more widely spread.
metas.footer: Source: posted by unfazed on The Real Meta Research Group (RMRG) Discord

metas.name: India - Landscape - Andhra Pradesh - Red Soil
metas.note:
Andhra Pradesh has a long coast along the bay of Bengal and it is fairly recognizable because of the red soil combined with overall flatness. This is the area in which you fill find red soil in Andhra Pradesh.

Flat landscape with red soil and lots of Palmyra should pretty much always give the eastern India coast.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Anisun River Valley
metas.note: A rocky desert can be found in this valley southwest of Nandyala, AP.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Assam - Hilliness
metas.note: Hilliness in Assam is found mostly South or East of Nagaon.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Assam - North Mountains
metas.note: If you see Mountains to the North in Assam, you're on the border to Arunachal Pradesh. In my experience, this is a particularly common sight on the border east of Itanagar.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Badvel Valley
metas.note:
Wind turbines aligned on top of mountain ranges are very common in these mountain ranges valleys I would say. (I know there are some in RJ as well)

Even without wind turbines, you can click in this valley if you have a good north/south angle. I would even say that it is the only place in India with such big N/S dry ranges to the west AND to the east.

Differentiations:

  • Western ghats mountains in Maharashtra (Pune-Nashik area) have different angles
  • The other Mountain Range in Andhra Pradesh (near Odisha border) is less dry.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Chaukhamba
metas.note: Chaukhamba, located near the town of Ukhimath, is a mountain massif covered in snow which can be recognised by its three distinct peaks, with the centre peak being the tallest.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Coastal Andhra Pradesh
metas.note:
Coastal Andhra Pradesh is characterized by a flat, agricultural landscape with coastal bushes

50/50 Tip ! Similar bushes can also be found in Gujarat, but Gujarat will often have distinct holey poles or have a boxy car. Also, Gujarat will primarily have date palms whereas Andhra will have palmyra palms as the main occurrence in palm trees.

The harder rounds in Andhra are the coastal, agricultural ones without any Palmyra or any pole. This basically becomes a 50/50 with any other flat & agricultural state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dark Soil
metas.note: Distinctly dark soil is mainly found in Maharashtra and adjacent regions.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dark Soil - Karnataka
metas.note:
Dark soil in India is usually found in and around Maharashtra.

In many cases you can see trident poles together with this dark soil, which will put you in Northern Karnataka, usually near the Maha border (free 4.5k+)

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dry Ganges River Valley
metas.note: Southern Haryana and Southern Uttar Pradesh are very agricultural, but often still look dry. These areas look like a mix of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dry Mountains
metas.note: In Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh you can find an extremely dry landscape with little to no vegetation within the Himalayan mountains.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dry TG/AP
metas.note: If you have a Telangana/Andra pole or Telugu with a dry landscape, you are likely in the area between Anantapur, AP and Shadnagar, TG (see image)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Elevated Dry Road
metas.note: Elevated Roads (similar to Bangladesh), with a dry landscape, are common in and around Jharkhand.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Elevated Jammu & Kashmir
metas.note: While a lot of the coverage in Jammu is located in flat parts, there are some areas north and northeast of the city of Jammu with elevation, where you will be able to see a lot of pines.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Ganges River Valley
metas.note:
The northern plains, also known as the Ganges River Valley, of India are very fertile with extremely flat and open agricultural fields.

Note by MB: Agriculture can be found in many parts of India. I think what sets apart these Northern Plains is the lack of palm trees (except for the occasional date palms and the Palmyra palm spam in Bihar).

metas.name: India - Landscape - Gujarat - Dead Landscape
metas.note:
Salt flats and coastal marshes with nearly no vegetation, other than short yellow or brown grass, can be found in parts of Gujarat. Shallow bodies of water can often be seen around these areas.

NOTE: The soil in western Rajasthan will be a lot more sandy and you’ll typically be able to see short desert shrubs.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Guntur Landscape
metas.note:
Around Guntur in Andhra Pradesh, you can find a landscape that combines the Andhra Pradesh Panhandle and the agricultural east coast further south.

You will have lots of agriculture (more than in Panhandle) and also many palm trees (more than in the coastal region further south).

metas.name: India - Landscape - Haryana - North Haryana vibes
metas.note:
The northern part of Haryana is very green and agricultural.

Note by MB: Ganges River Valley in general looks like this, but I feel like this area is even greener and lusher, and it also has more sugarcane.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Himachal Pradesh - North/South Valley
metas.note:
The city of Manali is fairly recognizable due to it being one of the two areas with coverage in a recognizable north-south valley. The other is from Kullu to Nagwain 50 km south of it.

The only way I came up with to tell the 2 apart is the vegetation but this is kinda fake since both cities are located in the same valley.

According to me, Manali has poplar trees and pines within the city whereas the other area doesn’t have much of those and mostly consists of random trees.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Himalayas
metas.note: The by far tallest mountains in India are found in the Himalayas.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Ladakh - Snow Coverage
metas.note: Coverage extends to roads that are very high in altitude, so snow can be visible on the end of the streetview east of Leh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Madhya - Elevated
metas.note: There are a few places where you can have elevation in Madhya Pradesh. The main elevation areas are around Yawal and satpura park, as well as south of Indore
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Madhya Pradesh - Red Soil
metas.note: Within Madhya Pradesh, a reddish or pinkish soil is generally more common towards the East.
metas.footer: Source: self-researched by Jayden and me

metas.name: India - Landscape - Maharashtra West Coast
metas.note: The landscape west of the Western Ghatts in Maharashtra is quite unique. It has a lot of forests, and a dark brown soil. It's mostly a vibe thing, but it looks kinda like Kerala but with less palms.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Mechuka Valley
metas.note: The Mechuka valley is the only place in Northeast India where snowy mountains are visible. The valley contains brownish grass and a plethora of Bhutan white pine. North of Mechuka the coverage gradually becomes overcast and somewhat dark.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Meghalaya Hills
metas.note: The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded, smooth hillsides with a flat top.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Mizoram Hills
metas.note: The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded hillsides having many small peaks scattered around.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Monoliths
metas.note: Near the southern tip of Tamil Nadu, you can find these large monolithic mountains, with huge exposed rocks. Several of these mountains can be seen from afar, especially the Magenthiragiri hills.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Mountains in Tamil Nadu
metas.note: Mountains in Tamil Nadu can be found along the western border. Additionally, there's a lot of mountains west of Madurai and some east of Salem.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - NH3 between Gramphu and Dalang
metas.note: This section of road features huge mountains, with a little bit more **green on their slopes. **
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Panhandle Andhra Pradesh
metas.note:
The panhandle of Andhra Pradesh looks quite different than the rest of the state. It is much greener (and has an arguably "darker greener" tone). There are also A LOT more coconut palms here than anywhere else in AP.

Other parts of Andhra Pradesh do have Palmyra Palms, but Coconut palms are kinda rare outside of the panhandle.

The area south of Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh can also look extremely similar, but it has a lot less coverage.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Punjab - Elevated
metas.note: Punjab is generally a very flat state. If you know you're in Punjab, but it's hilly or mountains, you're on the border to Himachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan - Mountains
metas.note: The biggest mountainous areas in Rajasthan are around Alwar max northeast and Udaipur - Mount Abu area
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan - NorthEast Ridge
metas.note: In Rajasthan, there is a North-east angled ridge going from Mount Abu area to New Delhi
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan - Rolling Hills
metas.note: In Rajasthan, rolling hills are common for the area south of Udaipur
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan Vibes
metas.note: Rajasthan is a state that is drier than its surrounding states. It's difficult to explain, but many locs in Rajasthan just have a certain 'drier' vibe. If you saw this loc and thought 'This looks like Rajasthan', pat yourself on the back :)

metas.name: India - Landscape - Red soil
metas.note: Red soil can be found in several regions, but mainly near the southern west coast and in and around Chhattisgarh and western Odisha.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rewa Ridge
metas.note: A pretty straight east-west range with a slight north east angle can be found near Rewa. It is fairly easy to recognize.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rockiness
metas.note:
Telangana and Andra Pradesh have a lot of “rockiness”. It can be rocks on the side of the road, boulders or even rocky hill slopes but they share that in common.

I found it to be more in Telangana so the meta is here, but note that it can extend to surrounding states of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.

Note by MB: In my experience, in AP, rockiness is very common west of the ridge from Tirupati to Nallamala Forest.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rural Manipur Landscape
metas.note:
Since Imphal is located in a valley, it is fairly simple to recognize it after a few games.

The landscape around the city consists of agricultural fields surrounded by mountains, so it is pretty easy to know you are in Imphal.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Snow Coverage in the Mountains
metas.note:
This coverage can be found on the 3 in Himachal Pradesh near the Ladakh border.

The coverange extends from Zing Zing Bar to Killingsarai

metas.name: India - Landscape - Southern Tamil Nadu Red Soil
metas.note: A flat, bushy landscape with very red soil can be found in southern Tamil Nadu.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Spiti River Valley
metas.note:
The shape of the mountains iin this valley are truly unique : very dry, very high in elevation and sparsely green.

If you have trouble making the difference between this road and the NH3 to the west because it looks roughly similar, just know that the NH3 is paved whilst the Spiti river valley roads usually are not.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Tirupati
metas.note: The city of Tirupati, AP can easily be recognized by the huge ridge in the North. Other metas, like black&yellow Tuk-Tuks, two-indent poles or simply Telugu language, can help confirm.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Ganges River Valley
metas.note: The western Ganges River Valley (Punjab/Haryana/Western UP) usually looks wetter and greener than the general Ganges River Valley. You can often see rice and sugarcane. Note that areas like this can still be found in other parts of the river valley, this is not a 100% meta

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Ghats
metas.note:
The Western Ghats Mountains in the western part of Maharashtra can be recognised by their distinct ridgelines, often having plateaus rather than peaks. The northern part is drier while the southern part has more vegetation.

NOTE: During the rainy season the mountains will turn green and appear quite different.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Meghalaya Landscape
metas.note:
The western part of Meghalaya basically looks like bangladesh with hills. There are a lot of areca palms, banana trees and palms.

“Hilly forests with areca palms surrounding flat agricultural fields” is how I would best describe this part of Meghalaya.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Rajasthan Landscape
metas.note: The western parts of Rajasthan can commonly be recognised by the dry landscape with sandy soil.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Uttarakhand Landscape
metas.note: The western half of Uttarakhand is typically far more barren than the other Himalayan regions, due to logging and erosion. The coverage northwest of Dehradun on the Himachal Pradesh Border has some especially barren hills full of brown grass and small roads next to cliffs.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Wonky Hills
metas.note: The Odisha Hills are very "wonky", i.e. they're undulating and can also very greatly in height.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary
metas.note: Unique hilly landscape with dead trees. Note that not all coverage in this park looks like this.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Dryness
metas.note:
The Nusas typically look drier than other regions in Indonesia. The islands get especially dry towards the east, especially in Generation 3. Vegetation tends to look less tropical, but instead more brown with a lack of leaves. Sumba Island is also the driest of the Nusas.

NOTE: While less common, other regions such as Java can look similarly dry. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Lake Toba
metas.note: The region around Lake Toba, in North Sumatra, can be recognized by mountains surrounding the lake and Samosir Island in the middle. Overcast coverage is also common for the region.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Palu Bay
metas.note: Palu Bay is a unique slightly north-west facing bay just north of Palu city, which features mountains to the west of the bay, and a flat, more urbanised landscape to the east.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Red Soil
metas.note: Red soil can often be found on Batam and the Bangka Belitung islands, located east of mainland Sumatra.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Savannah
metas.note:
This savannah landscape is occasionally seen on North Sumba.

NOTE: In Generation 3, you will always see a white car.

metas.name: Japan - Landscape - Mount Fuji
metas.note:
Mount Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan, with a gradual incline and often snowy summit.

Depending on the elevation, it can be seen from far away. This can create some excellent region guesses, especially if you account for direction and distance.

metas.name: Japan - Landscape - Plains
metas.note:
Japan is notably a very mountainous country. However, there are some regions that are quite flat, being the Nobi and Kanto plains. While at times they can look very similar, determining that it is one or the other can be very helpful.

NOTE: While there are, of course, other flat areas in Japan, these two are the most recognizable.

metas.name: Landscape - 35
metas.note: Road 35 is surrounded by hills and mountains, and the ground is mostly covered in green shrubs. Curved lamp posts are posted at regular intervals on the northeastern side of the road.

metas.name: Landscape - 45 south of Mudayy
metas.note: Most of Road 45 south of Mudayy is unpaved and goes generally north to south, through some very rough hilly terrain. The soil is light and very rocky. Beware that the southernmost stretch is paved.

metas.name: Landscape - Adam Ridge
metas.note: Just north of Adam, you’ll find a flat desert landscape with greyish soil and mountains in the distance, notably one long ridge to the south followed by two smaller and rounder hills to the east and southeast. Other mountains are also visible to the north and west.

metas.name: Landscape - Al Amarat
metas.note: If you are surrounded by mountains on all sides, and you are in a somewhat urban area, you are likely just southeast of Muscat, in Al Amarat.

metas.name: Landscape - Bidiyah Landscape - Dunes
metas.note: South of Bidiyah you can find a couple of dirt roads going through a slightly rolling landscape consisting of orange-pink sand and small yellow-ish shrubs. The roads mainly go between long and low sand dunes with a general south-south-west direction.

metas.name: Landscape - Bidiyah Landscape - Flat
metas.note: Sandy desert with light coloured green and yellow shrubs can be found in northeastern Oman, mainly south and west of Bidiyah.

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal 41
metas.note: Coastal Road 41 features one of the sandiest landscapes in Oman, with very light sand all around. The coast is sometimes visible in the distance.

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal 41 - Ridge
metas.note: Coastal Road 41 features one of the sandiest landscapes in Oman, with very light sand all around. The coast is sometimes visible in the distance. On the north-to-south stretch, you can see a distant ridge to the west.

metas.name: Landscape - Dry Mountains
metas.note: Northern Oman features a dry mountainous landscape similar to eastern UAE. The south coast of Oman also rarely features some similar mountains.

metas.name: Landscape - Masirah
metas.note: Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.

metas.name: Landscape - Masirah - 51
metas.note: Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. Road 51, which circulates the island, usually only has a white centre road line, which can help in recognising it. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.

metas.name: Landscape - Max South 45
metas.note: Most of Road 45 south of Mudayy is unpaved and goes generally north to south, through some very rough hilly terrain. The soil is light and very rocky. Beware that the southernmost stretch is paved.

metas.name: Landscape - Musandam
metas.note: Most of the coverage in the Musandam Governorate exclave is coastal, with rocky cliffs usually hugging the road. A majority, but not all, of this coverage will have the coast to the west, excluding any other roads in the country with a similar look.

metas.name: Landscape - Narrow 32
metas.note: Going further north, Road 32 travels through a hilly desert landscape, in a general northern direction.

metas.name: Landscape - Nizwa Mountains
metas.note: The mountains north of Nizwa have an amount of green bushes that are unusually large for the north. The mountains are very rocky and jagged, which differentiates them from the more rolling mountains in the south.

metas.name: Landscape - North of Al Awaya Road
metas.note: The road north of Al Awaya features a desert landscape with dark grey soil, which is not common in the south. The road itself still has the orange tint characteristic of southwest Oman.

metas.name: Landscape - North of Al Mazyunah Road
metas.note: The unpaved road north of Al Mazyunah, near the Yemen border, has a north-north-west bound angle, and the desert has sandy, red-tinted sand, which still has some shrubbery around. You can see some hills in the distance. The southwards driving direction and sunny weather can be used as confirmation.

metas.name: Landscape - Orange Sanddunes
metas.note:
A road going through large orange-pink sand dunes can be found north of Fasad.

NOTE: The same dunes can be seen in the distance close to the northern part of the Yemen border.

metas.name: Landscape - Orocue Road
metas.note: This road leading from the 65 to the town of Orocue is characterized by its unique angle and the orange/brown dirt.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Landscape - Rolling Hills
metas.note: Close to the southern coast, especially around Salalah, you will find a rolling hills landscape. The area commonly features rocky ground, bushes and small trees as well as some fairly green valleys.

metas.name: Landscape - Sadah Coastal Road
metas.note: Road 42/49 east of Salalah is a scenic coastal road that features a lot of light-coloured tall rocky cliffs. The coast is also often visible.

metas.name: Landscape - Salalah Plains
metas.note: Salalah is located on a flat coastal plain with rolling mountains surrounding it to the north.

metas.name: Landscape - Ubar Fields
metas.note: Around the town of Ubar, you can find patches of green agricultural land surrounded by desert.

metas.name: Landscape - Western 41
metas.note: The western stretch of Road 41 has wide shoulders similar to Road 31, however, the more northwest-bound angle along with the reddish soil should tell them apart.

metas.name: Landscape - Wide 32
metas.note: Crossing into the Ash Sharqiyah North Governorate, the shoulders become wide, like those on Road 31. However, unlike Road 31, the desert here is darker and has more shrubs and greenery. A long portion of the road also has overcast coverage. The lighter red section is no longer road 32 but still features the wide shoulders. The landscape further north also gets hillier and more vegetated.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Cerro del Bernal
metas.note: Cerro del Bernal is a distinct extinct volcano that is found in southern Tamaulipas. It can be found heading directly northwest of Tampico or west of Morón.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Ciudad Juarez
metas.note: The outskirts of Ciudad Juárez features a lot of dirt roads with a distinct shade of orange soil and low shrubs.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Ciudad Obregon
metas.note: The area around Ciudad Obregon is distinct due to the pinkish-tan soil and canals found around the city’s agricultural areas.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Guaymas Cliffs
metas.note: The town of Guaymas has a lot of jagged cliffs and mountains that make the area very distinct. The soil is also distinctly pinkish and organ-pipe cacti can be seen scattered on the hills and next to the road.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Maderas del Carmen
metas.note:
This tall, flat ridge, with very prominent ridgelines, belongs to the Maderas del Carmen Biosphere Reserve in Northern Coahuila near the US border.

NOTE: The only road the mountain range can be observed from is the Federal Highway 53 that leads to Boquillas del Carmen.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - MEX-40D
metas.note: The 40D that crosses the Sinaloa-Durango state line is recognizable by the stunning lush cliffs and mountains along the road. The highway commonly passes through tunnels and the road itself features double yellow middle roadlines.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - MEX-54
metas.note: The 54 is a divided highway that runs through northeastern Zacatecas which features yucca trees spammed on both sides of the road. Additionally, the streetview car is often exposed and appears almost white due to the sunlight.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Mexicali Landscape
metas.note: The area around Mexicali features flat farmland with a ridge to the west. Washingtonia palms are very common and these poles made out of brown wood can be found.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Monterrey Mountains
metas.note: The Monterrey metropolitan area features tall stunning mountain ranges that surround the city.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Morelos Prickly Pear Farms
metas.note: Farms of prickly pear are commonly found in north east Morelos, where they foreground **striking, sculpturally eroded dry hills. **

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Northern Baja Landscape
metas.note: These reddish brown-tinged hills, often accompanied by large boulders, are a common sight for the northern half of Baja California.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Pink Lakes
metas.note: The town of Los Coloradas is famously known for the pink lakes around the area.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca
metas.note: The area around San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca and south of it in Oaxaca often feature rolling hills with really distinct orange and beige-tinged soil, passing from one colour to the other with each hill. The beige-tinged soil can be seen more prominent in some locations.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Sierra del Abra Tanchipa
metas.note: This extremely long and flat ridge is found in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve in eastern San Luis Potosi.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Twin Volcanoes
metas.note: The twin volcanoes of Iztaccíhuatl and Popocatépetl are found on the border between the State of Mexico and Puebla. Keep in mind that they are usually much less visible than depicted in the image, which is just for reference.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Western Chi/Dur Landscape
metas.note: The western parts of Chihuahua and Durango can feature a rocky mountainous landscape covered with pine forests. In general, these pines are shorter and more stunted in appearance than pine forests of the central or south.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - White Soil
metas.note:
Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.

NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - 82 (Andoya)
metas.note: The 82 on the island of Andoya, which is part of the Lofoten archipelago, is flat apart from one tabletop looking hill. In generall, the hills on this road are quite unique and recognizable. You will find short scrubs along the road. Often, you will be able to see water.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Atlanterhavsveien
metas.note:
This road uses dark rocks as bridges. You will see water on both sides of the road. The coverage features dark clouds.

The road includes the famous Storseisundet bridge.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy
