metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Deep Fjords
metas.note: While fjords can be found along most of the Norwegian coast, deep fjords surrounded by tall mountains are most common between Bergen and Trondheim.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - E10 in Lofoten
metas.note: This road features huge mountains. It is a skinny road that has water to the east. Lots of sections have bridges or open tunnels. You will frequently find fireweed on the sides of the road. The vegetation on this road has a yellowish tone.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - E10 on the border of Troms and Nordland
metas.note: This road runs through a valley. You can see a big mountain range along the road, with no trees on the mountain. Some sections are very green, and some section feature fireweed.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - E10, East of Narvik
metas.note: This road is very green and usually features big mountains with no trees. Right on the Swedish border you will find parts without trees.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - End of the World Road
metas.note: This famous road can be identified by the lack of trees and the small white rocks. The visibility in the coverage is somewhat low. Some sections are very flat, while others can have small hills and lakes.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Exposed Rock
metas.note: Exposed rock, often spotted with small coastal pines and bushes, is mainly found on the south coast.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Highlands
metas.note: Barren highlands, with no trees or bushes, and often with rocky mountains along the road, are mostly found in the southwest.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Lofoten Mountains
metas.note: Distinct, sharp, rocky mountains with few trees can be seen on the Lofoten Archipelago.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Lysevegen
metas.note: Lysevegen is a very windy and skinny road with 28 180° turns down the mountain. Notably, there are big power lines visible. You can see huge mountains in the distance. The coverage is very cloudy.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Northeastern Landscape
metas.note: The northeast of Norway can typically be recognized by a somewhat rolling landscape, rather than tall mountains, and vegetation mainly consisting of very small birches combined with patched grass.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Northern Coastal Grasslands
metas.note: Coastal grasslands with little to no other vegetation and only somewhat low, distant mountains can be found by coastal roads in the far north.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Oslo Farmlands
metas.note: The largest concentration of farmland is found in the southeast, in the general vicinity of Oslo. The area is much flatter than most of the country, and it is common to get a rolling landscape with smooth, round forested hills in the distance. The area southeast of Oslo is particularly flat.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Røst Island
metas.note: This island has only Gen 2 coverage. You will see lots of boats everywhere. The landscape is flat and islandish (duh).
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Russian Border Road
metas.note: Along the Russian border you can see this noticeably humid and green-looking road, with very overcast and occasionally foggy coverage. The trees are somewhat low and mainly consist of thin birches and pines.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Stavanger Farmlands
metas.note: The farmland south of Stavanger is flatter than most of the country. The fields look vast and open, and it is very common to see rock walls made of large, round rocks. Furthermore, rather than crops, most fields will only contain grass.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Trollstigen
metas.note: Trollstigen leads down a huge mountain, and is surrounded by such. The road is very steep and windy. The rock is very dark and has green moss on it. Some sections are cut into the rock, with waterfalls appearing.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Trondheim Farmlands
metas.note: The farmlands surrounding Trondheim are generally very hilly, and the hills are typically both steeper and more uneven than in the southeast.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - 1N (Piura - Lambayeque)
metas.note: The 1N near the Piura and Lambayeque border has a distinct looking landscape. It features a semidesert landscape and has overcast coverage in Generation 3. The new Generation 4 is drier but still looks somewhat similar.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - 1S (Coastal)
metas.note: The 1S south of the city of Ica is not divided and mostly follows the coast. The soil is often red or orange in these areas, and there is little-to-no vegetation. This road is also entirely covered with the Generation 4 camera.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - 28B
metas.note: Ruta 28B between the towns of Kimbiri and Echarate is a paved road with very faded or missing road lines. It is also characterised by being a relatively small road with Generation 4 coverage, which hugs the hillside and is located next to a river valley.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - 30C
metas.note: Ruta 30C in eastern Peru uses a white Street View car in Generation 3 between the cities of Planchon and Iñapari. It features dense forest, few villages, and resembles interior areas of Brazil. Some of this area has been overwritten with Generation 4. Most of this segment runs north to south.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - 5N (San Alejandro - Esperanza)
metas.note: Ruta 5N between the towns of San Alejandro and Esperanza is a relatively straight, flat road in good condition. This road primarily runs north-south through the rainforest.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Atacama Desert
metas.note: Areas near the cities of Ica, Arequipa, and Tacna feature barren and mostly flat desert landscapes that can resemble areas of northern Chile. You can typically see mountains in the distance, primarily while looking to the east.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Cusco
metas.note: The southern city of Cusco is recognizable by its prevalence of both red brick and Spanish colonial style buildings. Cusco is surrounded by mountains on all sides and features an airport in the middle of the city. Due to its proximity and similar architecture, Cusco superficially resembles the Bolivian city of La Paz.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Exposed Rock Outcroppings
metas.note:
In higher elevation areas near the centre of the country, exposed rocky outcroppings are commonly seen in the sides of hills and mountains. Some areas with the highest concentrations are near Lago Chinchaycocha (Junin District) stretching south towards the city of Ayacucho.

NOTE: Exposed rocks can rarely be seen anywhere in the country, so use this meta with some caution.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Flat Landscape between Mountains
metas.note:
A flat landscape in the mountains of Peru is usually seen in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.

NOTE: This landscape might look similar to Bolivia. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Iquitos
metas.note: Iquitos is a city in northeast Peru. It is an isolated city with only Generation 3 Street View coverage. Three-wheeled tuk-tuks, overcast skies, and rolling Amazonian landscapes are commonly seen in the area. This coverage is isolated from other areas of northern Peru.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Iquitos Road
metas.note: The road to Iquitos can be recognized by black car Gen 3, lack of center lines and rolling Amazonian landscape
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Jauja Valley
metas.note: The valley connecting the cities of Jauja and Huancayo features a flat plain with plentiful trees, agricultural areas, and small villages. North-south oriented mountains can be seen on both edges of the valley.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Lake Chinchaycocha
metas.note: North of the city of Huancayo lies a shallow lake called Lake Chinchaycocha (also referred to as ‘the middle lake.’). This lake is generally marshy and a range of mountains can be seen to the east of the lake. This lake can look similar to Lake Titicaca, but is generally less densely populated and features fewer trees.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Lichen
metas.note: Patches of light green lichen can be seen covering rocks and growing on the ground in high elevation areas of central and southern Peru.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - North of Titicaca Wetness
metas.note: The coverage on the north side of Lake Titicaca was taken during a significantly wetter season than the coverage taken on the south side of Lake Titicaca.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Northern Amazonian Landscape
metas.note: The areas adjacent to the northern Amazonian city of Tarapoto feature moderately tall foliage-covered mountains and can bear a similar resemblance to the hilly areas of Colombia or Brazil.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Northwestern Piura Landscape
metas.note: The landscape northwest of the city of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is hilly, which distinguishes it from other Piura regions.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Red Soil
metas.note: Dark red-tinted soil is found in several areas of Peru. Some notable areas include the areas near Cusco and Ayacucho in the south of the country, as well as areas near the northern cities of Cajamarca and Tarapoto. It can be found to a lesser extent in adjacent regions.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Sandwiched Agriculture
metas.note:
Coastal agricultural valleys in the middle and south are commonly sandwiched between dry mountains with no vegetation. The general orientation of these valleys are southwest-northeast.

NOTE: Agricultural valleys in the north of Peru can look similar, but often feature more shrubs and trees on the mountains.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Sharp Mountains
metas.note: Similarly, taller mountains near the middle of the country often feature rocky and sharp mountain tops. The main region of these mountains stretches from near the city of Huaraz southward to the city of Cusco; generally away from the coast.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Shrubby Mountains
metas.note: Far north Peru features mountains that are often covered in shrubby trees and bushes. Closer to the coast and the Ecuador border, these mountains are often quite dry in appearance.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Southwestern Piura Landscape
metas.note: The southwestern landscape of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is mostly flat, but you will sometimes see rolling hills.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Tacna Ridge
metas.note: The city of Tacna in the far south of Peru has this distinct dry ridge to the north.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Titicaca Villages
metas.note: Low grass, a few hills, stone walls in villages and brown brick buildings are typical for the region south of Lake Titicaca in eastern Peru.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Tumbes Landscape
metas.note:
These three landscapes are typically found along offroads in Tumbes. You will always see sandy soil with either green or withered bushes.

NOTE: In addition, Tumbes does not have black cars on off roads. Make sure to consider it whenever you see such landscapes with a white Street View car.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Volcanoes
metas.note:
Volcanoes are often seen in and around the city of Arequipa.

NOTE: Within Peru, volcanoes are only found in the southeast in the highlighted area.

metas.name: Philippines - Landscape - Arayat Volcano
metas.note: The Arayat Volcano can be recognised by being completely surrounded by flat agricultural fields.

metas.name: Philippines - Landscape - Chocolate Hills
metas.note: On central Bohol you can find these distinct round grassy hills. The hills generally have dark brown soil beneath the grass, earning them the name of Chocolate Hills.

metas.name: Philippines - Landscape - Mayon Volcano
metas.note: The Mayon Volcano is one of the tallest mountains in the Philippines and can be recognised by its almost perfect smooth cone shape. Beware that it will very often be covered in clouds.

metas.name: Philippines - Landscape - Northern Luzon Landscape
metas.note: The forested mountain range in Northern Luzon is characterised by somewhat dry mountainsides and an abundance of pine trees. You may rarely come across a similar landscape on high-altitude roads in Mindanao.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Cape Town Mountains
metas.note: The distinct Table Mountain, located west of Cape Town, can be recognized by its prominent three-kilometre plateau. It is flanked by Devil’s Peak, which is more pyramidal.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - George Mountains
metas.note: Mountains in the Witfontein Nature Reserve, likely George’s Peak, will be visible north from the city of George.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Kruger National Park
metas.note:
The landscape around Kruger National Park is generally flat, with a savannah climate and dry vegetation. You will not see any agriculture and the vegetation is mostly made up of grasses, with small trees dotting the landscape. Red soil can also be seen below the grass.

NOTE: Within the coverage of the park, you will mostly find unpaved gravel roads or small and paved roads without road lines.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Northeastern Dry Season
metas.note:
The northeast of the country can look very dry and somewhat barren, with a lot of orange or red soil. You will often see hills or mountains covered in shrubs.

NOTE: Depending on the season, the coverage can change drastically from dry to very green.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Northern Cape
metas.note:
A dry landscape with red soil is typically found in the Northern Cape.

NOTE: This map is a useful guide in guessing based on the climate of South Africa.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - R360 North of Bokspits
metas.note:
The section of the R360 north of Bokspits, next to the Botswana border, has asphalt with a recognizable reddish tint. The landscape is arid and features dry greyish trees, shrubs and long golden grass. The road runs in a general north to south direction.

NOTE: Asphalt with a reddish tint can be found on other roads and the southern part of the R360. However, the landscape north of Bokspits looks predominantly like this.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Rocky Mountains
metas.note:
Unique rocky, treeless mountains can be seen in Western Cape, with most of the mountains having tall, steep sides and sharp peaks.

NOTE: Similar mountains can be seen in and around Lesotho.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Rolling Hills
metas.note: Grassy rolling hills are generally located in the coastal area of Western Cape between Cape Town and George, and just north of Cape Town. Tall ridges are usually visible to the north or east.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - South of Mozambique
metas.note: The landscape near the Mozambique border in the highlighted area is noticeably flat, with green subtropical vegetation.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Cliff Valley
metas.note: River valleys surrounded by steep, barren and rocky cliff sides can be found between the cities of Erzurum and Artvin and in the southeast near the city of Hakkâri.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Göreme Monoliths
metas.note: Göreme, west of Kayseri, can be recognised by the tall sandstone monoliths with ancient dwellings carved into them.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Grassland
metas.note: In the northeast you will find uncultivated grasslands in valleys surrounded by round hills. Trees are very limited in the region. In Generation 3 the area has an extremely distinct look, with deep green grass covering the hills. It is significantly more difficult to recognise in Generation 4, where the grass has a more arid look.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Lake Beysehir
metas.note: Along the western shore of Lake Beyşehir and Lake Eğirdir you can find this small single lane road with jagged, exposed rock and Turkish pines to the west. These two can be differentiated by the road west of Lake Eğirdir having a middle road line.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Lake Egirdir
metas.note: Along the western shore of Lake Beyşehir and Lake Eğirdir you can find this small single lane road with jagged, exposed rock and Turkish pines to the west. These two can be differentiated by the road west of Lake Eğirdir having a middle road line.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Lake Van
metas.note: Lake Van is by far the biggest lake in Turkey and has a semi-arid landscape, being surrounded by dry grassy hills and occasional trees and agricultural fields near the shore.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Lush
metas.note: Northern Turkey tends to be significantly lusher and more forested than the rest of the country.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Mount Ararat
metas.note: Mount Ararat, labelled as Ağrı Dağı on Google Maps, is a dormant volcano in far eastern Turkey and the tallest mountain in the country. It is often seen together with Küçük Ağrı, a smaller volcano to the southeast.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Volcanic Rocks
metas.note: Dark, volcanic rocks are commonly found between the cities of Şanlıurfa and Diyarbakır.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Appalachian/Southern Hybrid
metas.note: Tennessee and Kentucky look like a mix of Appalachian and Southern Landscape.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Appalachians
metas.note:
The Appalachian mountain range is a low mountain range that runs through the eastern states. The general landscape consists of low, forested mountains, with beech and oak trees being a common sight.

NOTE: Houses in the south generally have less storeys. New England architecture, commonly consisting of wood panelling, high roofs and a porch, is also more common toward the north, especially in New England.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Badlands
metas.note: Badlands National Park features these distinct, sand-brown, eroded rock formations. The formations may sometimes appear more rounded, and lighter in colour.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Big Bend National Park
metas.note: Big Bend National Park is located along the Mexico border in Southwest Texas. It can be identified by its dry, rocky peaks and shrubby foliage. This park is adjacent to the Chihauhan desert, so plants such as yucca and prickly pear cactus are common.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Black Hills
metas.note:
The Black Hills, located in far Western South Dakota and far Eastern Wyoming, are a series of moderately tall mountains with large amounts of conifer trees and rocky outcroppings. The surrounding areas are typically much flatter with lesser tree cover.

NOTE: This area has a similar appearance to many areas within the Rocky Mountains, which lie further to the West.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Canadian Landscape (Maine)
metas.note: Landscapes vary quite a bit in New England. Maine in particular can look a lot like Canada.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Central Appalachians
metas.note: In the Appalachian area stretching from southern New York to southern Virginia, there are a lot of forest-covered rolling hills, with flat valleys dividing them. A majority of the ridges are oriented Southwest to Northeast.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Central Florida
metas.note: The soil gets a little more sandy in Central Florida. There are also more pine trees than palms (they’re occasionally seen too).
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Central Valley
metas.note:
Central Valley, California can be recognized by its Mediterranean climate. This is reflected in its agriculture, seen in the vineyards and olive trees that can commonly be found here.

In addition, rolling hills can be seen toward the edges of the valley.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Circular Lakes
metas.note: Small circular shallow lakes are especially common in Central Florida around Lakeland and Orlando.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Colorado Ridge
metas.note: Central Colorado is home to a large North-to-South oriented mountain ridge. This divides the Rocky Mountains to the west and the Great Plains to the east.These mountains are adjacent to the major metropolitan areas of Boulder, Denver, and Colorado Springs.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Death Valley
metas.note:
Death Valley National Park can be easily recognized by the dry, sandy, treeless mountains that can be seen from the roads that go through the park. In Generation 3 coverage, the sky can look particularly dusty.

NOTE: Many smaller roads in Death Valley only have Generation 1 coverage.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Devil's Tower
metas.note: In far Northeastern Wyoming lies Devil’s Tower, which is a very tall, standalone butte protruding from the surrounding land. This can sometimes be seen from many miles away because of the lack of nearby mountains.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Driftless Area
metas.note: The driftless area in Southwestern Wisconsin is quite unique. It has features of Midwestern States (for example agriculture), but is very hilly.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Everglades
metas.note: Deep South Florida, between the metropolitan areas of Ft. Myers and Miami, features dense, jungle-like forests that have few inhabitants. Roads through these areas are commonly very straight and long.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Florida Jungle
metas.note: Deep South Florida, between the metropolitan areas of Ft. Myers and Miami, features dense, jungle-like forests that have few inhabitants. Roads through these areas are commonly very straight and long.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Florida Keys
metas.note:
The Florida Keys are an archipelago of tropical islands west of Miami. The highway connecting the islands can be recognized by green, tropical vegetation on the sides of the usually single lane road. The soil is also sandy white.

Urban locations are also similar, but with many more planted palm trees and mowed grass being a common sight.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Glacier National Park
metas.note:
Along the Canadian border in Montana lies Glacier National Park. It is easily recognizable by its extremely tall and steep mountain peaks. Most coverage is also hazy and taken during summer.

NOTE: Other National Parks within the Rocky Mountain range of the US can have a similar appearance, so consider other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Great Basin
metas.note: The Great Basin, centred around Nevada, can be recognized by the tall, sometimes snow-capped mountains in the background. There are dry, but grassy, and slightly shrubby plains leading up to the mountains.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Great Basin - Green
metas.note: Within the Great Basin, greener mountains can be seen in Idaho and central Utah.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Great Basin - Oregon
metas.note: Within the Great Basin, more gradual, rocky hills can be seen in Oregon.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Great Plains
metas.note: The Great Plains are in the middle of the United States and stretch from the Canadian border in the North, to central Texas in the South. This area is primarily flat with few trees. Some areas feature agriculture fields, while others feature dry and barren grassy fields.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Guadaloupe Foothills
metas.note: In adjacent areas of New Mexico and Texas, smaller foothills of the Guadaloupe Mountains can be seen with relatively flat tops and shrubby foliage.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Guadalupe Mountains
metas.note: Along the New Mexico and or Texas border there is a ridge of tall, dry peaks known as the Guadalupe Mountains. In adjacent areas of both states, smaller foothills of these mountains can be seen with relatively flat tops and shrubby foliage.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Louisiana
metas.note: Flat and marshy landscapes are a common sight in Louisiana.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Lush Spruce Forest
metas.note: Spruce and pine forests are a common sight in the western United States in New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and to the west of those states. The lush spruce forest types shown become increasingly common near the Pacific coast in Washington, Oregon, and California.
metas.footer: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Mid-Atlantic Agricultural
metas.note: Some locations in the Mid-Atlantic region can look deceivingly Midwestern but with more trees.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Mid-Atlantic Forest
metas.note: Upstate New York and Pennsylvania are quite forested. Rolling hills are also common.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Mississippi River Valley
metas.note: The Lower Mississippi River Valley is a very flat and open landscape with red soil in areas of Tennessee, Arkansas, Mississippi, and Northeast Louisiana. Corn and other crops are common in this area.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Nebraska Sandhills
metas.note: The Nebraska Sandhills are a recognizable region of rolling hills covered with prairie grass in the central-north part of the state.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - New England
metas.note: Landscapes vary quite a bit in New England. Maine in particular can look a lot like Canada if you know your countries in GeoGuessr. The topography of New England is mostly rolling hills. The forests are littered with fir trees and aspens.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Northern California
metas.note: One thing that sets NoCal apart from SoCal is the amount of palm trees. You generally see palms everywhere in the LA area but hardly any in the San Francisco Bay Area.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Northern Florida
metas.note: North Florida has sandier soil and rarely has any palm trees. Most forests are pine forests and the vibes feel more like Florida’s neighbors to the north than Florida itself.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Oklahoma Peaks
metas.note: Southwestern Oklahoma features a small area of rocky, shrubby peaks. Some of the mountains are also covered in trees, and the rocks can have a pinkish red tint to them.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Ouachita Mountains
metas.note: The Ouachita Mountains stretch from Eastern Oklahoma into West-Central Arkansas. Unlike the nearby Ozark Mountains, these mountains are typically more steep in nature and easier to see from a distance.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Pacific Rainforest
metas.note:
Temperate rainforests are found in coastal areas of Washington, Oregon, and Northern California. These rainforests feature many broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns.

NOTE: These rainforests stretch north into coastal British Columbia and Southeast Alaska as well.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Pine Forest Hills
metas.note: Spruce and pine forests are a common sight in the western United States in New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and to the west of those states. The landscape that you can see in the picture meanwhile can be found in the states of Colorado, Montana, Wyoming, Utah, New Mexico, Arizona, Idaho, some locations in Nevada, and the eastern portions of Oregon, Washington, and California.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Prairie Pothole
metas.note: The area spanning from the Montana Border with Saskatchewan to the Western Great Lakes features many ‘prairie potholes.’ These are areas of low-lying wetlands that feature marshy grasses and small, shallow ponds.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Reddish Soil
metas.note:
You’ll find red soil everywhere in the South. The area where red soil can be found stretches all the way from some parts of Louisiana and Arkansas all the way to southern Virginia through Mississippi, southern Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina, and North Carolina.

The Oklahoma City region in Oklahoma is also notable for its red soil.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Rio Grande Valley
metas.note: The Rio Grande Valley in South Texas is extremely flat and features shrubby trees and agricultural fields. This area borders the Mexican state of Tamaulipas.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Rocky Mountains
metas.note: The area stretching from the Canadian border to Northern New Mexico is home to the Rocky Mountains. These jagged, rocky formations often feature many pine trees and visible snow all-year round at the highest peaks. Some areas of the Rocky Mountain Range are noticeably dry, with few trees.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Rolling Hills in Florida
metas.note: The area between the cities of Orlando and Lakeland in Florida sometimes feature low, rolling hills. Lakes and agricultural fields are also common in this area. This is the only main hilly area in central or southern Florida.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Roosevelt National Park
metas.note:
Theodore Roosevelt National Park features similar, sand-brown, eroded rock formations to Badlands National Park. The rock formations in this park tend to have more trees on them. Additionally, almost all coverage has fall colours visible.

NOTE: Similar formations can be seen in far eastern Montana as well.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Rural New Jersey
metas.note: Rural New Jersey looks strikingly southern.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Shiprock
metas.note: Shiprock is a rock formation and a municipality in northwestern New Mexico. This striking, isolated mountain is visible from distances of up to 40 km (roughly the red square) and is therefore a good clue for identifying the region within the Navajo Nation. Similar rock formations can be seen around Shiprock, but they do not have a long, low stone wall next to them.
metas.footer: Source: Meta of the Day on the German GeoGuessr Discord

metas.name: United States - Landscape - South Florida
metas.note: South Florida is marshy and tropical. You’ll see an abundance of palm trees here.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Southern California - Rural
metas.note: Southern California outside the major cities of Los Angeles and San Diego is a barren desert.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Southern California - Urban
metas.note: In general Los Angeles and San Diego feel more tropical and the houses are more spread out as opposed to the more compact and dense feel of San Francisco.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Spruce/Pine Forest
metas.note: Spruce and pine forests are a common sight in the western United States in New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and to the west of those states.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Tablelands
metas.note: The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, feature many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Texas Hills
metas.note: Just west of the metropolitan areas of Austin and San Antonio Texas lies a large area of dry, rocky hills featuring many yucca and prickly pear plants. Texas Live Oak trees are the predominant tree type in this area.
